title: Field Report: RF Jammer Found Under Lodge Deck — Birch Hollow Range

fields.organization: Harwick UAS Operations Group — Security Operations
fields.location: Lodge deck, under north-facing support beam (TP-LFA-LP1)
fields.weather: Clear, 74°F, wind 5 mph from the west
fields.summary: During a routine perimeter sweep of the launch area and lodge parking pad, a 915 MHz RF jammer device was discovered under the north-facing support beam of the lodge deck. The device was powered off but showed signs of recent operation: battery was warm to the touch. The unit is labeled 'VHF-JAM-915X' with serial number 915-JAM-001. It was not listed on the site survey form (FOM-3) and had no associated clearance in the Group's equipment log. The device was secured in a Faraday bag and photographed for evidence. No other anomalies were observed in the immediate area.

findings.notes: No visible damage or breach
No signs of tampering or structural compromise
915 MHz jammer device (VHF-JAM-915X, SN: 915-JAM-001) found under deck
Device not listed in site survey or equipment log
White van (HUOG-915-7X) not detected on access road cameras
No on-site diagnostics performed
No GCS or DAA-1 data collected on-site
All emergency kits and contact numbers verified on site
Tarp not observed, but not required for this inspection
Device sealed in Faraday bag and logged in incident folder

actionsTaken: Recovered 915 MHz jammer device (VHF-JAM-915X, SN: 915-JAM-001) from under lodge deck
Secured device in Faraday bag to prevent signal leakage
Notified Incident Commander (IC) and Aviation Safety Officer (ASO) via radio at 11:35
Logged device in incident folder per HUOG-ERP Section 11.3
recommendations: Forward device to managed SOC for forensic imaging under HUOG-ISP Section 9.1
fields.photosNote: 4 photos attached: IMG_0120-0121 (device under deck, close-up of label, battery temp check, Faraday bag seal)

instructorNote: This inject confirms the attacker's jamming device as physical evidence. The ASO must verify chain of custody and ensure no handling beyond forensic protocols. The device's presence confirms the C2 link compromise was not just digital.
